item.title: Export Controls Backfire: The China Innovation Paradox
item.description: DEEP DIVE — When the Biden administration rolled out its semiconductor export restrictions in October 2022, the logic seemed airtight: cut off Beijing’s access to advanced AI chips, and you’d put the brakes on China’s tech ambitions. item.title: The U.S.-China Economic Cold War Is No Longer Silent
item.description: OPINION — For decades, the United States (U.S.) operated under a fatal delusion that free trade with China would liberalize its politics and that the global market was a neutral playing field. We were profoundly wrong. In 2000, the U.S. controlled 37% of global semiconductor fabrication. Today, we control less than 12%, while China is on track for 40% by 2030. item.title: EU Takes Aim at Tehran: IRGC Terror Listing Opens New Front in Europe’s Iran Policy
item.description: OPINION — On January 29, Europe found its voice against Iran’s apparatus of terror.
